overview.heading: How the Real Estate Listing Photo Editor works
paragraphs: Upload a photo of a room or the front of a property, choose one of four edits and, if you like, add a short direction such as a furniture style. PiCraft returns an edited version in the same 4:3 landscape format that most listing sites expect, with the architecture, windows and floors left as they are.

Enhance brightens and straightens a photo that was taken quickly. Declutter removes loose items such as personal belongings and surface clutter. Virtual staging furnishes an empty room, and virtual twilight turns a daytime exterior into a warm dusk photo.

Edits to listing photos come with responsibilities: most MLS systems and some states require you to label altered images and keep the original. The page below explains what to check before you publish.

whatYouGet.title: 2048×1536 px MLS image
whatYouGet.description: A landscape 4:3 JPG at a size that suits most MLS systems.

whatYouGet.title: 1600×1200 px web version
whatYouGet.description: A lighter JPG kept under 1 MB for your website, social posts and email.

whatYouGet.title: Four kinds of edit
whatYouGet.description: Enhance, declutter, virtual staging and virtual twilight, each applied to your own photo.

whatYouGet.title: Optional style direction
whatYouGet.description: Add a short note, such as "Scandinavian living room, light oak and white", to steer furniture and mood.

whatYouGet.title: Structure kept intact
whatYouGet.description: The model is told to keep walls, windows, floors and the layout as they are, so the image still shows the real property.

useCases.title: Listings from phone photos
useCases.description: Agents and owners who photograph a home themselves can brighten and straighten the images before posting.

useCases.title: Empty rooms
useCases.description: Show how an unfurnished living room, bedroom or office could be used, with a clear staged label on the listing.

useCases.title: Cluttered rooms
useCases.description: Remove temporary clutter such as toys and counter items so buyers see the space itself.

useCases.title: Exteriors at dusk
useCases.description: Turn a flat daytime shot of the front of the house into a warm evening photo for the lead image.

useCases.title: Rentals and short-term stays
useCases.description: Improve photos for rental listings and vacation rentals where a professional photographer is not worth the cost.

tips.title: Shoot from a corner
tips.description: Stand in a corner at about chest height so you capture as much of the room as possible with straight vertical lines.

tips.title: Turn the lights on and open the blinds
tips.description: A bright, evenly lit source photo gives the best result. Very dark or blurry photos cannot be saved.

tips.title: Hold the camera level
tips.description: Tilted walls and sloping floors carry through into the result. Use the grid lines on your phone.

tips.title: Use one edit per photo
tips.description: Declutter first, then run the cleaned image through virtual staging if you need both. Mixing goals in one pass gives less predictable results.

tips.title: Add a style note for staging
tips.description: A short direction such as "modern, light wood, neutral colors" keeps the furniture appropriate to the property and the market.

tips.title: Compare before and after
tips.description: Put the two images side by side and check doors, windows, flooring and anything permanent. Nothing structural should change.

tips.title: Keep the original
tips.description: Save the unedited photo with each edited one. Many listing rules ask you to provide it.

styleGuide.heading: Choosing an edit
styleGuide.intro: Each edit solves a different problem. Pick the lightest one that does the job.

items.title: Enhance (bright & straight)
items.description: For well-composed photos that are a bit dark, tilted or dull. The least invasive option.

items.title: Declutter
items.description: Removes loose items and clutter. Use it for lived-in rooms, and never to hide damage.

items.title: Virtual staging
items.description: Adds furniture and décor to an empty room. It must be labeled on the listing.

items.title: Virtual twilight (exterior)
items.description: Converts a daytime exterior into a dusk photo with warm window light. Use it for the lead image of a house.

checklist.heading: Before you publish an edited listing photo
items: Label every virtually staged or materially altered image the way your MLS requires, in the photo description, on the image or in the remarks.
Provide the unaltered original alongside the edited image where your MLS asks for it.
Check that walls, floors, windows, fixtures, views and the surrounding area still match the real property.
Confirm that nothing has been removed or hidden that a buyer would reasonably want to know about, such as damage, stains or cracks.
Check your MLS and state rules, because the required wording and placement of the label differ.
Use virtual staging only on empty or lightly furnished rooms, and say so in the listing text.
Keep both the original and the edited file in the property record.

limits: The edit must not misrepresent the property. Do not use it to hide defects or to change permanent features such as flooring, walls, windows or views.
Results depend on the source photo. Dark, blurry or heavily tilted photos give weaker results.
Virtual staging places furniture in a plausible way, but sizes and layouts are approximate and are not an architectural plan.
Each photo is a separate generation and uses one credit. The maker does not process a whole property in one pass.
Rules on labeling edited photos differ by MLS and by state. PiCraft cannot tell you what applies to your listing.
